name: Drake Meats Federally Inspected Processing Plant — Saskatoon
description: Drake Meats is building a 53,000-square-foot federally inspected meat processing plant near Saskatoon capable of producing 8 million kilograms of pork and beef product annually. The project is financed by senior debt from Farm Credit Canada and equity from the Golden Opportunities Fund. Expected completion is between June and September 2026, with 70 to 80 initial employees scaling to 200 at full operation.
summary: Drake Meats is building a 53,000-square-foot federally inspected meat processing plant near Saskatoon capable of producing 8 million kilograms of pork and beef product annually.

evidence.title: Canada's Drake Meats Building New Facility in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan
evidence.snippet: 53,000-square-foot facility capable of producing 8 million kg of product annually; financed via Farm Credit Canada senior debt plus Golden Opportunities Fund equity.

evidence.title: Saskatchewan meat company builds new plant
evidence.snippet: Drake Meats to build CAD$50-60 million federally inspected plant in Saskatoon.

name: Beretta Farms Meat Processing Facility Expansion — Lacombe
description: Beretta Farms invested $10.9 million to expand its Lacombe, Alberta federally registered harvesting and meat processing facility by 10,000 square feet, adding warehousing, cooler space and office space. The expansion increases annual slaughter capacity from 29,583 to 44,688 head of cattle and received an Alberta Agri-Processing Investment Tax Credit of $1,228,735.
summary: Beretta Farms invested $10.9 million to expand its Lacombe meat processing facility, increasing cattle slaughter capacity from 29,583 to 44,688 head per year.

name: Kap Paper Medium-Density Fibreboard (MDF) Facility Conversion — Kapuskasing
description: The federal government is investing $7.5 million through the Strategic Response Fund for Kap Paper Inc. to complete a Front End Engineering Design (FEED) study for a medium-density fibreboard (MDF) facility conversion at the existing Kapuskasing mill. A prior $10 million FedNor investment was announced in October 2025. Conversion is forecast to take as little as 30 months once financing is in place; full capex described as 'hundreds of millions of dollars.'
summary: Federal Strategic Response Fund backing $7.5M FEED study for Kap Paper's conversion of its Kapuskasing pulp mill into a medium-density fibreboard facility.

name: Windsor Street Exchange Redevelopment — Halifax
description: Halifax is redeveloping the Windsor Street Exchange interchange to increase capacity for transportation and Halifax Water's wastewater collection. Total project cost is approximately $180 million, up from $47 million in 2019. Federal government is contributing $28 million under Build Canada Strong, plus $23.5 million via Transport Canada's National Trade Corridor Fund. Province of Nova Scotia contributes $10.75 million, Port of Halifax $2 million, and HRM approximately $85 million. Expected completion December 2029.
summary: Halifax's $180 million Windsor Street Exchange redevelopment expands road capacity and wastewater collection, with federal, provincial, port, and municipal funding confirmed.

evidence.title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Windsor Street Exchange Redevelopment Project in Halifax
evidence.snippet: $28 million federal investment in Windsor Street Exchange Redevelopment Project to increase wastewater collection capacity.

name: Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydroelectric Project
proponent: Nukkiksautiit Corporation (Qulliq Energy Corporation / Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated)
description: A proposed 15-30 megawatt hydroelectric facility along the Kuugaluk River approximately 60 kilometres northeast of Iqaluit that would replace the city's diesel-generated electricity. Cost estimated between $400 million and $500 million. On November 13, 2025, Prime Minister Carney added the project to the federal Major Projects Office nation-building list. Federal government invested $6 million in early-stage support. Construction targeted to begin in 2028 with potential operation by 2030.
summary: Proposed 15-30 MW hydroelectric facility on the Kuugaluk River to replace Iqaluit's diesel generation, referred to the federal Major Projects Office in November 2025.

evidence.title: Iqaluit Nukkiksautiit Hydroelectric Project referred to the Major Projects Office
evidence.snippet: Project referred to the federal Major Projects Office as part of the nation-building list.

evidence.title: Federal government invests $6M into Iqaluit hydro project

name: Kugluktuk Power Plant Replacement
description: Qulliq Energy Corporation awarded a $74.4 million contract to Pilitak Enterprises to replace the Kugluktuk power plant originally installed in 1968. Approximately 50% of funding comes from the federal Arctic Energy Fund. The new plant is designed to support renewable energy integration.
summary: Qulliq Energy Corporation awarded Pilitak Enterprises a $74.4 million contract to replace Kugluktuk's 1968 diesel power plant with a facility designed for renewable integration.

name: 99 King Street Rental Housing Development — Saint John
description: A 152-unit residential development in Uptown Saint John with two levels of underground parking, a floor of retail and commercial space, and 32 affordable units reserved for seniors and people with disabilities. Funded by $46 million from the federal government (CMHC Apartment Construction Loan Program), $2.1 million from the Province of New Brunswick, and $310,000 from the City of Saint John. Completion targeted for October 2026.
summary: 152-unit rental housing project at 99 King Street in Uptown Saint John backed by $55 million in combined federal, provincial, and municipal funding; completion targeted October 2026.

name: CFB Gagetown Range and Training Area Recapitalization
description: The Department of National Defence is investing $871 million to recapitalize the Range and Training Area at 5th Canadian Division Support Base Gagetown. The project is one component of a broader $1 billion-plus investment at CFB Gagetown that also includes $172 million for new ground-based air defence infrastructure and a $20.2 million transition-services building.
summary: DND allocated $871 million to recapitalize the Range and Training Area at CFB Gagetown as part of a broader $1 billion-plus base investment package.

name: Canadian Armed Forces Military Housing Expansion Phase 2 — National
proponent: Department of National Defence / Canadian Forces Housing Agency
description: The Minister of National Defence launched Phase 2 of Canada's national military housing construction program in February 2026. The program will deliver approximately 7,500 new Residential Housing Units across 25 sites in six regions, valued at more than $3.7 billion. The initiative is part of a broader CAF housing strategy.

name: Carpere Canada AI Health Town / Valley View Data Centre — Moose Jaw
proponent: Carpere Canada / Carpere Valley Development Corporation
description: Carpere Canada is proposing a $485 million mixed-use redevelopment of the former Valley View Centre site in Moose Jaw, combining a 150 MW data centre with an AI wellness centre, a regenerative medicine facility, a nursing training school, and home-care services. Waste heat from the data centre will warm a nearby greenhouse. Phase 1 construction could begin in late 2025 or early 2026; total buildout 5 to 8 years. Carpere plans to self-finance the initiative.
summary: $485 million Carpere Canada redevelopment of Moose Jaw's former Valley View Centre combining a 150 MW data centre with AI-enabled health and training facilities.

name: Fish Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade — Calgary
description: The City of Calgary awarded Graham Construction a $547,125,000 contract to upgrade the Fish Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant. The upgrade will improve efficiency, increase capacity, add the first Alberta heat recovery system of its kind, and reduce emissions by 1,600 tonnes CO2 annually. Construction scheduled from 2025 to 2031. Plant serves approximately 280,000 Calgarians.
summary: Calgary awarded Graham Construction a $547 million contract to upgrade the Fish Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant with a first-in-Alberta wastewater heat recovery system; construction runs 2025-2031.

name: North End Sewage Treatment Plant (NEWPCC) Phase 3 — Nutrient Removal Facility
description: The third and final phase of Winnipeg's North End Sewage Treatment Plant upgrade — a new nutrient removal facility — has a cost estimate of $1.491 billion. Winnipeg's draft 2026 budget sets aside $547 million toward the project, the primary driver of a 76% increase in the city's 2026 capital budget. Full project requires $1 billion in additional funding to proceed.
summary: Third phase of Winnipeg's North End Sewage Treatment Plant upgrade — a nutrient removal facility — estimated at $1.491 billion with $547 million earmarked in the city's 2026 draft budget.

name: Route 90 / Kenaston Boulevard Widening and St. James Bridges Replacement — Winnipeg
description: The City of Winnipeg's Route 90 improvement project widens Kenaston Boulevard, rebuilds the St. James bridges over the Assiniboine River, and replaces combined sewers along the corridor. Preliminary design estimates construction at $586 million plus $151 million in interest, for $737 million total. Recommended schedule has construction starting in 2028 and completing before 2033.

name: Highway 107 Twinning — Burnside to Loon Lake
proponent: Nova Scotia Department of Public Works
description: Nova Scotia is twinning Highway 107 from Burnside to west of Loon Lake in the Halifax Regional Municipality. Construction on the section between Burnside and southeast of Exit 14 (Montague Road) began in 2024 with completion expected 2028-2029. The project is one of six major highway construction projects announced by the province with a combined $583 million commitment for 2025-2030.

name: Nunavut Housing Agreement in Principle — 750 Homes
proponent: Government of Nunavut / Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated / Government of Canada
description: On January 30, 2026, the Government of Canada, Government of Nunavut, and Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated signed an Agreement in Principle to deliver up to 750 public, affordable, and supportive homes across Nunavut. Up to $250 million from the federal government and up to $230 million from the Government of Nunavut.

name: Canada Games Aquatic Centre Upgrade — Saint John
description: The City of Saint John plans upgrades to the Canada Games Aquatic Centre ahead of hosting the 2029 Canada Games. Plans include a warm-up pool and additional seating. Construction is targeted to begin in summer 2026 with completion in summer 2028.
summary: Saint John plans upgrades to the Canada Games Aquatic Centre ahead of hosting the 2029 Canada Games; construction targeted summer 2026 to summer 2028.
